A manufacturing plant produced 1288 units of a product during the period. Its standard costing system set the following per-unit standards for direct material and direct labor:

Direct material standard: 6 lb per unit at a standard price of $18/lb.
Direct labor standard: 2.92 hours per unit at a standard rate of $40/hour.

Actual results for the period: 7695.4 lb of material were purchased and used (assume no beginning or ending material inventory) at an actual price of $15.52/lb, and 3600.8 direct labor hours were worked at an actual rate of $43.96/hour.

Formulas (sign convention: a positive variance is unfavorable -- actual cost exceeded standard; a negative variance is favorable):
- Standard Quantity Allowed = standard quantity per unit x actual units produced.
- Standard Hours Allowed = standard hours per unit x actual units produced.
- Material Price Variance = (Actual Price - Standard Price) x Actual Quantity Used.
- Material Usage (Quantity) Variance = (Actual Quantity Used - Standard Quantity Allowed) x Standard Price.
- Labor Rate Variance = (Actual Rate - Standard Rate) x Actual Hours Used.
- Labor Efficiency Variance = (Actual Hours Used - Standard Hours Allowed) x Standard Rate.

Compute, in this order: (1) Material Price Variance, (2) Material Usage Variance, (3) Labor Rate Variance, (4) Labor Efficiency Variance -- each in dollars, rounded to 2 decimal places (positive = unfavorable, negative = favorable).
